name: Interchangeable parts watchmaking
summary: A factory method in which machines cut every part to a gauge, so that a part from one watch fits any other watch of the same model.
how: Cut each part on a machine to a gauge of 0.01 mm.
Sort the parts into bins by model, not by watch.
Assemble the watch from parts that the worker does not file or fit.

origin.note: The Boston Watch Company builds a factory for machine-made watches.

adoptions.via: The Waltham firm makes watches with machine-cut parts and sells them at a price that railroad workers can pay.
